The **Fields Medal** is a prize awarded to two, three, or four [mathematicians](Mathematician "Mathematician") under 40 years of age at the [International Congress](International_Congress_of_Mathematicians "International Congress of Mathematicians") of the [International Mathematical Union](International_Mathematical_Union "International Mathematical Union") (IMU), a meeting that takes place every four years. The name of the award honours the Canadian mathematician [John Charles Fields](John_Charles_Fields "John Charles Fields").[[1]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-Fields_Institute_About_Us-1)

The Fields Medal is regarded as one of the highest honors a mathematician can receive, and has been [described as the Nobel Prize of Mathematics](List_of_prizes_known_as_the_Nobel_or_the_highest_honors_of_a_field "List of prizes known as the Nobel or the highest honors of a field"),[[2]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-:0-2)[[3]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-:2-3)[[4]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-:3-4) although there are several major differences, including frequency of award, number of awards, age limits, monetary value, and award criteria.[[5]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-5) According to the annual Academic Excellence Survey by [ARWU](Academic_Ranking_of_World_Universities "Academic Ranking of World Universities"), the Fields Medal is consistently regarded as the top award in the field of mathematics worldwide,[[6]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-6) and in another reputation survey conducted by [IREG](IREG_Observatory_on_Academic_Ranking_and_Excellence "IREG Observatory on Academic Ranking and Excellence") in 2013–14, the Fields Medal came closely after the [Abel Prize](Abel_Prize "Abel Prize") as the second most prestigious international award in mathematics.[[7]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-7)[[8]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-8)

The medal was first awarded in 1936 to Finnish mathematician [Lars Ahlfors](Lars_Ahlfors "Lars Ahlfors") and American mathematician [Jesse Douglas](Jesse_Douglas "Jesse Douglas"), and it has been awarded every four years since 1950. Its purpose is to give recognition and support to younger mathematical researchers who have made major contributions. In 2014, the Iranian mathematician [Maryam Mirzakhani](Maryam_Mirzakhani "Maryam Mirzakhani") became the first female Fields Medalist.[[11]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-Farsnews-11)[[12]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-12)[[13]](Fields_Medal#cite_note-13) In total, 64 people have been awarded the Fields Medal.

The most recent group of Fields Medalists received their awards on 5 July 2022 in an online event which was live-streamed from Helsinki, Finland.
